Scouts discloses autonomous drone monitoring at Vidullanka solar plants

New reports describe a September deployment combining 4K and thermal cameras with automated docking at two Sri Lankan solar facilities.

Colombo Gazette ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A first-customer deployment is disclosed

Reports published on October 8–9 describe Scouts’ aerial-monitoring installation for Vidullanka PLC in Sri Lanka. Deployment was completed in September, rather than on the reporting date. According to the partners, Vidullanka is the first customer of this autonomous system, which operates at two solar plants with a combined capacity of four megawatts.

An integrated monitoring service

The installation combines an automated drone, a weatherproof docking and charging station, and anomaly-detection software. Its 4K and thermal cameras support checks for damaged fencing, vegetation encroachment, maintenance needs and fire risks. Scouts describes locally managed hardware, software and services intended to provide situational information to personnel on the ground.

Operational evidence remains limited

The partners say aerial coverage can reduce continuous ground-patrol work and help staff respond. The reports do not provide flight counts, false-alarm rates or independently verified cost comparisons. This is an infrastructure deployment example, but it does not establish all-weather performance or demonstrate that security personnel can be replaced entirely.
